about: The offertory antiphon of the First Sunday of Advent, Psalm 24:1–3 in the Vulgate numbering (Psalm 25 in Hebrew). The missal prints here, word for word, the verses the introit sang.

s01.translation: To You I have lifted up my soul. My God, I trust in You: let me not be ashamed, nor let my enemies deride me; for indeed none who wait for You will be put to shame.

translation_citations.title: The Missal for the Laity (1846)
translation_citations.locator: parallel Ordinary and Advent propers, examined edition

w013.note: “Erubéscam” can express a plea, “let me not be put to shame,” or a future statement, “I will not be put to shame.” The Latin ending itself is shared by both readings.
w013.explanation: The psalmist asks that his trust in God not be disappointed. The Hebrew volitive form and Greek optative also support reading these words as a plea.
